mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) signals strong housing market activity, which is a leading indicator of consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.10% for two consecutive months, it signals an imminent monetary easing cycle that reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.10% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through a joint labor market strength effect.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high consumer confidence and strong housing activity, a rising residential construction permits (HOUST) signals continued demand momentum that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the money supply (as proxied by RSAFS) indicates expanding liquidity conditions that lower risk premiums and support equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS is rising, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 6.5% for three consecutive months, it signals an impending economic slowdown that increases equity risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6.5% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically precedes a period of equity market expansion as the central bank stabilizes the economy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime characterized by rising employment and falling unemployment, a sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market recovery that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during post-recession recovery when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.
